To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chronic pain is a disorder in which the pain network is ready for processing of pain.
patients with functional pain problems are characterized by intensified responses to pain symbols and that this is the more important characteristic than the intensified response to pain stimuli.
patients with functional chronic pain problems show intensified pain-related brain activity in response to noxious and near-noxic stimuli and that they are hypersensitive for pain symbols.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how pain words hurt.
the processing of pain signals and symbols and not with pain itself.
the question of why pain patients are more responsive to noxious stimuli than healthy individuals are.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study of pain symbols and signals is a promising and fruitful approach to understanding pain.
pain words hurt and that they might hurt in a way that they are not supposed to hurt.

pain words hurt, but not in a way as we would like to understand this in a strict pain experience but as a bias in processing of consequent stimuli and as an important step towards the development of a functional pain disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are still far away from a full understanding of the pain experience and its pathophysiological changes in patients with chronic pain but that we might be on the right track if we consider pain words and faces as important pain primes.
the study of pain symbols and signals in brain and behaviour is a promising approach in pain research.
pain symbols hurt.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pain symbols can do harm.
we should not be too focussed on pain words and facial displays of pain but should also take into account the role of pain symbols and pain faces as primers and preparators of pain.
we should not only study pain in the context of noxious stimuli but also pain symbols and pain primes.
